headline: Hawkish Fed tone tempers a winning week, retail sentiment stays split
body: Equities closed out the week under a light cloud after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address leaned more hawkish than markets had priced, flagging inflation still running near 3.7% year-over-year and putting a September rate move back on the table -- futures now imply roughly even odds of a hike next month. The S&P 500 slipped about a quarter percent to close near 7,712 on Friday and the Nasdaq gave back closer to half a percent, while the Dow was essentially flat. Treasury yields moved higher in response, with the two-year note touching its highest level since July, and the dollar firmed alongside it. Even so, all three major indices finished the week higher, extending a run of resilience despite the added rate-path uncertainty.

Retail positioning looks more mixed than directional. Stocktwits data shows sentiment on SPY improving to outright bullish even as sentiment on QQQ sits neutral, a split suggesting optimism is concentrated in broad-market exposure rather than the growth/tech names most sensitive to rate expectations. Chatter on WallStreetBets is dominated by sharp mention spikes in a handful of names -- PayPal and Palantir among them -- alongside steady AI-adjacent interest in names like Marvell and Alphabet, while Bitcoin mentions jumped roughly 9% in a single day, hinting at some rotation toward higher-beta, speculative exposure. Traders online seem genuinely divided on how to read Warsh's remarks, debating whether the market's calm reflects complacency about hawkish risk or just a squeeze on bearish positioning -- more uncertainty than conviction either way.
